collection.description: A wild boar has been raiding the gardens for a week: tearing up taro, flattening the beans and charging anyone who comes near.

ask.text:
A wild boar has been raiding the gardens for a week: tearing up taro, flattening the beans and charging anyone who comes near. The farmers are at their wits' end. (Name) has agreed to drive it off, with a fence of sharpened stakes and a lot of noise.
At dusk, (name) is waiting by the garden when the boar comes out of the trees. It's bigger than (he/she) expected, as big as a small canoe, and it stops, and lowers its head, and looks right at (him/her).
Should (name) stand (his/her) ground and shout, or climb the nearest tree?

c1o1.text: The boar crashes through the stakes, catches (name) with a tusk, and is gone into the trees. The healers stitch the wound, and it heals, but (name)'s leg is never strong again. (He/She) walks with a carved stick afterwards, and doesn't run anywhere, ever. But the boar never comes back to the gardens, and the farmers bring (name) the first of every harvest.

c1o2.text: Three steps from (name), the boar swerves, crashes through the stakes and bolts back into the forest, squealing. It never comes back. (Name) stands there with (his/her) pots raised, shaking, then sits down very suddenly in the beans. The farmers find (him/her) there, still holding the pots, and carry (him/her) home like a hero.

c1.text: (Name) bangs two pots together and yells at the top of (his/her) lungs. The boar paws the ground, snorts, and charges...

c2o1.text: The boar waits all night. Near dawn, (name) dozes off, and the branch (he/she) is on gives way. (He/She) lands badly, the boar flees at the noise, and (name)'s back is hurt in a way that never fully heals. (He/She) walks stiffly ever after, and the village builds (him/her) a raised bed so (he/she) needn't bend. (He/She) still goes to the garden every morning, to sit by the fence and glare at the forest.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c2o2.text: The boar gets bored by midnight and wanders off. (Name) climbs down at dawn, stiff and cold and covered in ant bites. (He/She) used to love running through the forest after tracks. After a night up a tree with a boar underneath, the thrill of running anywhere is gone. (He/She) leaves the boars to the fishers' dogs from then on.

c2.text: (Name) scrambles up the nearest tree just as the boar thunders past underneath. It circles the trunk, grunting, and settles down to wait...
